quote: You never really understand a person until you consider things from his point of view … until you climb into his skin and walk around in it.
source: Harper Lee, To Kill a Mockingbird, Part One, chapter 3 (Atticus Finch)
speaker: Atticus Finch, to Scout

evidence.where: Google Books snippets of the novel itself (Harper Lee, To Kill a Mockingbird, and the Enhanced Edition), plus SparkNotes and GradeSaver placing it in chapter 3
evidence.edition: To Kill a Mockingbird (J. B. Lippincott, 1960); Warner paperback 1982 pp. 29 to 30 as cited by McCutcheon
evidence.locator: Part One, chapter 3, Atticus to Scout on the porch the evening of her first school day

reason: The novel prints the sentence in two halves around Scout's interjection (point of view, a dash, Sir?, a dash, until you climb into his skin); the spaced ellipsis marks that omission and every word is Lee's. Not shipped, person at zero of three, not banned, and the speaker is named in the source.
